name: Trumpism
summary: Trumpism is the American right-wing populist movement built around Donald Trump and the 'Make America Great Again' slogan. It combines economic nationalism (tariffs, Buy American), immigration restriction, an America First foreign policy, social conservatism and hostility to the 'establishment', media and universities, with a strong, personalised executive. Scholars debate whether it is a coherent ideology or a style, and some describe illiberal or authoritarian tendencies.
scope: The mainstream movement as expressed in Trump's 2017 and 2025 inaugural addresses, the 2024 Republican platform and scholarly descriptions of the movement's components (right-wing populism, national conservatism, economic nationalism, Christian nationalism). Both Trump administrations are covered, with the second administration's foreign-policy record used for foreign-policy answers. Pre-2015 Republican orthodoxy, libertarian and neoconservative strands are not followed. Many economic and philosophical answers are low-confidence because the movement is thin and leader-centred. Defining scholarship used: Streich (Journal of Populism Studies), who treats Trumpism as a right-leaning populism led by Donald Trump's MAGA and America First movement; its own texts are the 2017 and 2025 inaugural addresses and the 2024 Republican platform adopted under Trump.

notes: Scholars disagree whether Trumpism is a coherent ideology; former adviser John Bolton says it lacks a philosophical core. Evangelical and Christian-nationalist strands, libertarian-leaning economic conservatives and nationalist-populist strands differ on abortion, welfare, same-sex marriage and the role of the state. Later pass (2026-11-13): answers resting only on Wikipedia, inferred answers and 0s recording adherent splits were nulled; answers kept state a position in the inaugural addresses or the 2024 platform. Themes searched in the saved texts: borders and immigration, trade, energy, military and alliances, education, religion, speech, elections, courts, welfare and pensions, crime, family, sex and gender, space. The platform and addresses are silent on most economic-system, philosophical, religious-doctrine and historical-theory statements, so those stay null; the uncertainty rule may exclude the ideology.
